item.content:encoded:
The AJA Foundation provides philanthropic funding to organizations working to create sustainable impact in three major areas: clean water, quality education and fundamental healthcare. The Foundation funds projects globally, with particular emphasis on initiatives that address essential needs and improve opportunities for underserved communities.

Important update: The AJA Foundation’s official application page currently states that invitations for new grants are paused and applicants should check back later in 2026 for updates. Therefore, this is not currently an open grant call.

About the AJA Foundation

The AJA Foundation seeks to address unequal access to essential resources by supporting organizations working in areas it considers fundamental human rights.

Its primary focus is on:

  • Clean and sustainable water
  • Quality education
  • Fundamental healthcare

The Foundation’s approach is centered on supporting organizations that can create sustainable and measurable impact for communities that lack access to essential resources.

Areas of Funding

1. Water

The Foundation supports sustainable water initiatives, particularly projects serving rural communities in Africa.

Its water work focuses on helping communities gain access to sustainable clean-water systems and improving the long-term health, social and economic conditions associated with access to water.

2. Education

The education pillar supports organizations helping disadvantaged students overcome financial or academic barriers.

Projects can focus on improving educational access and creating opportunities for students who may otherwise face significant obstacles to achieving their educational goals.

3. Healthcare

The healthcare pillar supports organizations delivering fundamental healthcare to underserved populations, particularly in developing countries.

The Foundation’s healthcare work includes support for organizations providing essential services in communities where access to healthcare is limited.

Who Can Be Considered?

The Foundation prioritizes organizations whose missions align with its philanthropic pillars and whose programmes demonstrate potential for sustainable impact.

Projects should fall within one or more of the Foundation’s focus areas:

  • Water
  • Education
  • Healthcare

The Foundation’s geographic service area is global, meaning projects can be located in different parts of the world.

How the Application Process Works

When applications are being accepted, the process begins with a short message to the Foundation explaining how an organization’s programme aligns with one of its philanthropic pillars.

The Foundation reviews the initial inquiry and may invite an organization to submit a full grant proposal if there is sufficient alignment with its mission and funding is available.

If invited to submit a full proposal, the organization receives instructions for accessing the online application and has 60 days to complete the submission.

A full proposal may take up to six months to review before a funding decision is made.

Letters of Intent

The Foundation’s published process states that Letters of Intent are generally accepted on a rolling basis, with no fixed application deadline, and applicants can expect a response in approximately six weeks.

However, the current application page specifically states that invitations for new grants are currently paused. Prospective applicants should therefore monitor the Foundation’s official website for the next update rather than assuming that a new application can currently be submitted.

Grant Amount

There is no single fixed grant amount stated by the Foundation.

Grant sizes vary depending on the programme, and the Foundation directs applicants to its funding history for examples of previous awards.

Recent funding records show awards across the three pillars, including grants to organizations working in Uganda, Zambia, Ethiopia, Guinea, Haiti and other locations. For example, the Foundation’s 2026 funding history lists a $600,000 UNICEF water grant for Guinea, a $400,000 grant to Makolekole in Zambia, and several education and healthcare grants.

Global Funding

The AJA Foundation funds projects globally. Its funding history demonstrates support for organizations across multiple countries and regions.

The Foundation’s stated impact includes investments in water, education and healthcare initiatives designed to address fundamental needs and expand access to opportunities.

What Organizations Should Prepare

Organizations interested in applying when new grant invitations reopen should be prepared to demonstrate:

  • A clear connection to water, education or healthcare.
  • A programme capable of creating sustainable impact.
  • The community or population the project serves.
  • The development challenge being addressed.
  • How the proposed work aligns with the Foundation’s philanthropic priorities.
  • The expected impact of the project.
  • Evidence of the organization’s ability to implement the proposed programme.

Applicants should always check the official application page for the latest requirements before submitting anything.

Current Application Status

Applications for new grant invitations are currently paused.

The Foundation advises prospective applicants to check back later in 2026 for updates.

How to Apply When Applications Reopen

Organizations should visit the official AJA Foundation application page for updates and instructions:

AJA Foundation – How to Apply

Applicants should not assume that the historical rolling-LOI process means applications are currently open, because the Foundation’s current page explicitly indicates that new grant invitations are paused.

Conclusion

The AJA Foundation Grants provide potential funding opportunities for organizations working to expand access to clean water, quality education and fundamental healthcare.

The Foundation funds projects globally and has supported a wide range of organizations addressing essential needs in underserved communities. Grant sizes vary depending on the programme and previous funding records demonstrate awards ranging from smaller project grants to substantial multi-year investments. (AJA Foundation)

However, organizations interested in applying should note that new grant invitations are currently paused. Prospective applicants should monitor the official AJA Foundation website for announcements later in 2026 and use the intervening period to prepare a strong project concept aligned with one of the Foundation’s three funding pillars.

Discover more opportunities on the OFY Webpage.

item.content:encoded:
Google has announced its February 2027 Apprenticeship opportunities for individuals seeking to develop practical, technical and professional skills in some of today’s most in-demand career fields.

The available opportunities cover Data Analytics, Digital Marketing, Project Management, Information Technology and User Experience (UX) Design. These programmes are designed for people interested in beginning a career in technology and related professional fields, particularly those with limited experience who want to gain structured training and practical workplace exposure.

Unlike conventional academic programmes, Google’s apprenticeships combine classroom-style technical instruction with hands-on work experience. Participants will train with a Google team, develop professional skills, receive career-development support and work toward a nationally recognised credential certified by the United States Department of Labor.

The apprenticeships are paid, full-time opportunities requiring participants to dedicate 40 hours per week to the programme. The programmes are expected to begin in February 2027 and last approximately 18 months.

Application deadline: September 21, 2026

Overview of the Google Apprenticeship Programme

Google’s apprenticeship programme is a structured learning and development pathway for individuals who want to enter a professional field but may not yet have extensive work experience or a directly related university degree.

The programme is registered with the United States Department of Labor and is designed to help apprentices build both technical and durable professional skills. Throughout the programme, participants receive a combination of:

  • On-the-job training.
  • Related technical instruction.
  • Track-specific learning.
  • Career-development workshops.
  • Professional mentoring and workplace exposure.
  • Career-readiness support.
  • Practical experience working with a Google team.
  • Preparation for future employment, education or other professional opportunities.

The programme begins with an immersive virtual onboarding experience. This onboarding period introduces apprentices to the profession, programme structure, expectations and foundational concepts related to their selected career track.

After onboarding, apprentices join a Google team and continue learning through practical assignments and supervised workplace training. They also participate in technical instruction and career workshops throughout the programme.

At the end of the apprenticeship, successful participants receive a nationally recognised credential certified by the United States Department of Labor.

Key Details at a Glance

  • Organisation: Google
  • Programme: Google Apprenticeship Programme
  • Start date: February 2027
  • Duration: Approximately 18 months
  • Work commitment: 40 hours per week
  • Programme format: On-the-job training, technical instruction and career development
  • Compensation: Paid hourly
  • Credential: Nationally recognised credential certified by the U.S. Department of Labor
  • Location: United States
  • Application requirement: Updated CV or résumé in English
  • Application deadline: September 21, 2026
  • Available fields: Data Analytics, Digital Marketing, Project Management, Information Technology and User Experience Design

The official listings state that participation requires applicants to be located in the United States for the duration of the apprenticeship programme.

Available Google Apprenticeship Opportunities

1. Google Data Analytics Apprenticeship

The Google Data Analytics Apprenticeship is designed for individuals who want to develop the skills needed to pursue an entry-level career in data analytics.

Data analytics involves collecting, organising, cleaning, examining and interpreting data to produce useful insights. Organisations use data analytics to understand performance, identify trends, solve problems, improve services and make informed decisions.

As a Data Analytics Apprentice, participants will learn how to move through the data lifecycle, beginning with data collection and preparation and progressing toward analysis, visualisation and the presentation of findings.

Skills and knowledge participants can develop

The apprenticeship will expose participants to foundational data analytics practices, including:

  • Understanding the data lifecycle.
  • Collecting and preparing data for analysis.
  • Cleaning datasets and identifying errors or inconsistencies.
  • Analysing data to identify trends, patterns and relationships.
  • Applying statistical methods.
  • Designing experiments and tests.
  • Using coding techniques for data analysis.
  • Creating data visualisations.
  • Presenting analytical findings to stakeholders.
  • Supporting data-driven decision-making.
  • Using tools such as SQL, Tableau and R.
  • Applying artificial intelligence tools and methods where appropriate.
  • Communicating technical findings in a clear and practical manner.

The programme is particularly relevant to individuals who enjoy working with information, solving analytical problems, identifying patterns and explaining what data means for organisations or business teams.

Main responsibilities

Data Analytics Apprentices may be expected to:

  • Analyse data to identify trends, patterns and insights that can support business impact.
  • Use statistical methods, coding and relevant artificial intelligence tools to conduct robust analysis.
  • Conduct statistical analysis and design experiments to identify useful insights.
  • Design tests that help answer business or operational questions.
  • Present data-driven findings, recommendations and solutions to partners and stakeholders.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams.
  • Practise responsible, effective and innovative use of artificial intelligence.

Compensation

The listed compensation range for the Data Analytics Apprenticeship is:

US$47,500–US$63,500, plus a 0% bonus target.

Individual pay is determined by factors such as job-related skills, experience, education and training.

Available locations

Applicants may have the opportunity to indicate their preferred working location from the following:

  • New York, New York
  • Atlanta, Georgia
  • Chicago, Illinois
  • Los Angeles, California

The role may also be located at Google’s Playa Vista campus in California.

Application link

Interested applicants can review the official listing and apply through the Google Data Analytics Apprenticeship, February 2027 Start.

2. Google Digital Marketing Apprenticeship

The Google Digital Marketing Apprenticeship is intended for individuals who want to develop entry-level skills in digital marketing, online advertising, campaign management, search engine optimisation and marketing analytics.

Digital marketing involves using online platforms, advertising channels, content, data and technology to reach audiences, promote products or services and achieve organisational goals. The apprenticeship will introduce participants to the planning, execution, optimisation and evaluation of digital marketing campaigns.

Apprentices will gain exposure to Google’s consumer and business products while learning how digital marketing strategies are developed and implemented across multiple channels.

Skills and knowledge participants can develop

The Digital Marketing Apprenticeship may help participants build knowledge in:

  • Digital marketing strategy.
  • Go-to-market planning.
  • Multi-channel campaign development.
  • Search advertising.
  • Video advertising.
  • Programmatic advertising.
  • Search engine optimisation.
  • Digital content and asset optimisation.
  • Campaign performance analysis.
  • Marketing metrics and reporting.
  • Client engagement.
  • Digital marketing technology.
  • Use of artificial intelligence tools to support creativity and efficiency.
  • Communication of marketing insights to clients and internal teams.

Participants will also learn how to monitor campaign performance and use data to determine whether marketing activities are achieving their intended objectives.

Main responsibilities

Digital Marketing Apprentices may be expected to:

  • Support the design and implementation of digital marketing strategies.
  • Assist with go-to-market activities and multi-channel campaigns.
  • Optimise campaigns and digital assets for search engine optimisation.
  • Use AI-powered tools where applicable to improve creativity, efficiency and campaign performance.
  • Support Search, Video and Programmatic campaigns.
  • Track important marketing and campaign metrics.
  • Analyse campaign data and prepare findings.
  • Present comprehensive results to clients and cross-functional teams.
  • Collaborate with colleagues and partners.
  • Practise responsible, effective and innovative use of artificial intelligence.

Compensation

The listed compensation range for the Digital Marketing Apprenticeship is:

US$47,500–US$63,500, plus a 0% bonus target.

Individual compensation may vary depending on relevant skills, experience, education and training.

Available locations

Applicants may indicate their preferred working location from:

  • New York, New York
  • Chicago, Illinois
  • Los Angeles, California

The role may also be located at Google’s Playa Vista campus in California.

Application link

Applicants can view the official listing and apply through the Google Digital Marketing Apprenticeship, February 2027 Start.

3. Google Project Management Apprenticeship

The Google Project Management Apprenticeship is designed for individuals interested in developing entry-level skills in project coordination, planning, task management, documentation, reporting and stakeholder communication.

Project management is essential in almost every industry because organisations need professionals who can coordinate people, resources, deadlines and activities to achieve specific goals. Project management apprentices will learn how to support projects and workstreams while developing the organisational and communication skills required in professional environments.

The programme will provide practical exposure to project-management processes and cross-functional collaboration.

Skills and knowledge participants can develop

The apprenticeship may help participants develop skills in:

  • Project planning.
  • Project coordination.
  • Task and workstream management.
  • Delegation.
  • Process documentation.
  • Progress tracking.
  • Reporting.
  • Stakeholder communication.
  • Cross-functional collaboration.
  • Problem-solving.
  • Identifying and addressing project roadblocks.
  • Process improvement.
  • Managing competing priorities.
  • Supporting timely project delivery.
  • Responsible use of artificial intelligence in project work.

Participants will learn how to organise project activities, communicate with relevant stakeholders and support teams in delivering work efficiently.

Main responsibilities

Project Management Apprentices may be expected to:

  • Work with cross-functional teams to manage project tasks and workstreams.
  • Support the coordination and delegation of project activities.
  • Apply project management skills such as planning, tracking, process documentation and reporting.
  • Communicate effectively with team members, partners and stakeholders.
  • Monitor progress toward project goals.
  • Proactively identify and address roadblocks.
  • Suggest improvements to existing processes.
  • Help manage stakeholder expectations.
  • Support timely project delivery.
  • Practise responsible, effective and innovative use of artificial intelligence.

Compensation

The listed compensation range for the Project Management Apprenticeship is:

US$54,000–US$72,000, plus a 0% bonus target.

Individual pay is determined by factors including job-related skills, experience, education and training.

Available locations

Applicants may have the opportunity to select their preferred working location from:

  • New York, New York
  • Atlanta, Georgia
  • Austin, Texas
  • Chicago, Illinois
  • Los Angeles, California

The role may also be located at Google’s Playa Vista campus in California.

Application link

Interested applicants can review the official listing and apply through the Google Project Management Apprenticeship, February 2027 Start.

4. Google Information Technology Apprenticeship

The Google Information Technology Apprenticeship is intended for individuals who want to build foundational technical skills and pursue an entry-level career in information technology.

Information technology professionals support the systems, devices, applications, networks and digital services that organisations depend on. The apprenticeship will provide practical training in areas such as device setup, hardware and software troubleshooting, network and cloud systems, IT security and end-user support.

The programme is suitable for people who enjoy solving technical problems, assisting users and learning how technology systems operate.

Skills and knowledge participants can develop

IT apprentices will develop foundational knowledge in:

  • Setting up and configuring devices.
  • Troubleshooting hardware and software.
  • Supporting operating systems and applications.
  • Managing or supporting network systems.
  • Understanding cloud systems.
  • Applying IT security policies.
  • Providing technical support to users.
  • Diagnosing technical problems.
  • Conducting root-cause analysis.
  • Supporting technology platforms and services.
  • Working with video and audio conferencing equipment.
  • Using AI and machine-learning tools where applicable.
  • Contributing to workflow automation.
  • Supporting process improvements.

The apprenticeship will help participants understand how technical problems can be identified, investigated and resolved in a professional workplace.

Main responsibilities

Information Technology Apprentices may be expected to:

  • Troubleshoot and resolve issues involving Google’s corporate resources, tools, operating systems and applications.
  • Provide local and remote technical support.
  • Conduct root-cause analysis of IT issues.
  • Support multiple technologies and platforms, including hardware, software, networks, tools and services.
  • Assist with integrated video and audio conferencing equipment.
  • Support end-user needs.
  • Contribute to IT projects involving workflow automation and process improvements.
  • Use relevant AI and machine-learning tools responsibly where applicable.
  • Practise responsible, effective and innovative use of artificial intelligence.

Compensation

The listed compensation range for the Information Technology Apprenticeship is:

US$47,500–US$63,500, plus a 0% bonus target.

Individual pay is determined by factors including job-related skills, experience, education and training.

Available locations

Applicants may indicate their preferred working location from:

  • Austin, Texas
  • New York, New York

Application link

Applicants can review the official listing and apply through the Google Information Technology Apprenticeship, February 2027 Start.

5. Google User Experience Design Apprenticeship

The Google User Experience Design Apprenticeship is designed for individuals who want to develop entry-level skills in user experience design.

User experience design focuses on understanding users, identifying their needs and challenges, and creating products or services that are useful, accessible and easy to use. UX professionals consider how people interact with digital products and work to make those interactions more effective and satisfying.

The apprenticeship will provide participants with practical exposure to UX principles, user research, design ideation, wireframing, prototyping and usability testing.

Skills and knowledge participants can develop

UX Design Apprentices may develop skills in:

  • User research.
  • Empathy and understanding user needs.
  • Identifying user pain points.
  • Defining design problems.
  • Ideation and solution development.
  • UX design principles.
  • Wireframing.
  • Prototyping.
  • Usability testing.
  • Gathering and applying user feedback.
  • Communicating design decisions.
  • Collaborating with product managers, software engineers and data scientists.
  • Designing accessible and user-centred products.
  • Using AI-powered tools for research, synthesis and prototyping where appropriate.

The official listing states that portfolios will not be collected or reviewed as part of the application process.

Main responsibilities

UX Design Apprentices may be expected to:

  • Empathise with users and understand their needs.
  • Define user problems and pain points.
  • Generate ideas for possible design solutions.
  • Apply UX best practices to real projects.
  • Create low-fidelity wireframes.
  • Develop high-fidelity prototypes.
  • Test designs and collect user feedback.
  • Improve designs based on research and testing.
  • Collaborate with product management, software engineering and data science teams.
  • Integrate user and business needs into design decisions.
  • Communicate design ideas and decisions effectively.
  • Practise responsible, effective and innovative use of artificial intelligence.

Compensation

The listed compensation range for the UX Design Apprenticeship is:

US$54,000–US$72,000, plus a 0% bonus target.

Individual pay is determined by factors such as job-related skills, experience, education and training.

Available location

The listed location for the UX Design Apprenticeship is:

  • New York, New York

Participation requires apprentices to be located in the United States for the duration of the programme.

Application link

Interested applicants can review the official listing and apply through the Google User Experience Design Apprenticeship, February 2027 Start.

General Minimum Qualifications

The minimum qualifications differ slightly depending on the apprenticeship track. However, the listed opportunities generally target individuals at the beginning of their professional journey.

Applicants should review the specific requirements for their preferred programme, but the general requirements include:

  • A high school diploma, GED equivalent or practical experience.
  • Less than one year of relevant experience in the selected field.
  • Applicants must not currently be enrolled in or have completed a bachelor’s, master’s or PhD programme in a degree field directly related to the selected apprenticeship.

The requirements for each track are outlined below.

Data Analytics

Applicants for the Data Analytics Apprenticeship should generally have:

  • A high school diploma, GED equivalent or practical experience.
  • Less than one year of relevant data analytics experience.
  • No current enrolment in or completion of a bachelor’s, master’s or PhD programme in data analytics or a related field.

Digital Marketing

Applicants for the Digital Marketing Apprenticeship should generally have:

  • A high school diploma, GED equivalent or practical experience.
  • Less than one year of relevant digital marketing experience.
  • No current enrolment in or completion of a bachelor’s, master’s or PhD programme in digital marketing or a related field.

Project Management

Applicants for the Project Management Apprenticeship should generally have:

  • A high school diploma, GED equivalent or practical experience.
  • Less than one year of relevant project management experience.
  • No current enrolment in or completion of a bachelor’s, master’s or PhD programme in project management or a related field.

Information Technology

Applicants for the Information Technology Apprenticeship should generally have:

  • A high school diploma, GED equivalent or practical experience.
  • Less than one year of relevant IT experience.
  • No current enrolment in or completion of a bachelor’s, master’s or PhD programme in an IT-related field, such as:
    • Information Systems.
    • Information Technology.
    • Applied Networking.
    • System Administration.

User Experience Design

Applicants for the UX Design Apprenticeship should generally have:

  • A high school diploma, GED equivalent or practical experience.
  • Less than one year of relevant UX design experience.
  • Experience gained through personal or professional projects, hobbies or online coursework may be considered.
  • No current enrolment in or completion of a bachelor’s, master’s or PhD programme in a design-related field.

The UX Design listing specifically states that portfolios will not be collected or reviewed.

Preferred Qualifications

In addition to the minimum qualifications, Google identifies several preferred qualities and skills that may help applicants succeed in the apprenticeship environment.

These include:

  • Experience using Google Workspace or a similar productivity suite.
  • Strong communication skills.
  • Good organisational abilities.
  • Problem-solving skills.
  • Critical thinking.
  • Customer-service skills.
  • Ability to work independently.
  • Ability to collaborate with others.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities.
  • Ability to navigate ambiguous tasks.
  • Willingness to seek help, guidance or advice when necessary.
  • A proactive and positive attitude.
  • Enthusiasm for new technologies.
  • Commitment to learning new skills.
  • Ability to adapt to changing tasks and professional situations.

Some tracks also identify additional preferred qualifications.

Additional qualifications for Data Analytics

Applicants may benefit from:

  • Personal data-related projects.
  • Familiarity with data analysis concepts.
  • Interest in statistics, coding or data visualisation.
  • Experience working with spreadsheets or analytical tools.
  • Interest in learning tools such as SQL, Tableau or R.

Additional qualifications for Digital Marketing

Applicants may benefit from:

  • Personal digital marketing projects.
  • Experience creating online content.
  • Familiarity with search engine optimisation.
  • Experience with social media or digital campaigns.
  • Interest in marketing analytics and advertising technology.

Additional qualifications for Project Management

Applicants may benefit from:

  • Experience coordinating projects or activities.
  • Experience organising events, programmes or group assignments.
  • Familiarity with task-management or productivity tools.
  • Evidence of strong planning and communication skills.
  • Experience working with teams or managing deadlines.

Additional qualifications for Information Technology

Applicants may benefit from:

  • Personal IT or technical projects.
  • Familiarity with coding languages.
  • Knowledge of operating systems.
  • Experience building or repairing computers.
  • Experience creating applications.
  • Volunteer experience with STEM organisations.
  • Practical experience troubleshooting technical problems.

Additional qualifications for UX Design

Applicants may benefit from:

  • Familiarity with design tools such as Sketch, Figma or Adobe applications.
  • Personal design projects.
  • Experience with wireframing or prototyping.
  • Interest in user research and usability.
  • Strong visual communication and problem-solving skills.

Programme Structure and Training Experience

Google’s apprenticeship programme is designed to combine practical work experience with structured learning.

1. Virtual onboarding

The programme begins with an immersive virtual onboarding experience. This stage helps apprentices understand the profession, the programme’s expectations and the foundational knowledge required for their selected track.

2. On-the-job training

After onboarding, apprentices join a Google team and begin practical workplace training. They learn by completing relevant tasks, participating in team activities and applying the knowledge gained through technical instruction.

3. Related technical instruction

Apprentices receive structured instruction related to their selected career field. This training is intended to strengthen their technical understanding and help them develop durable professional skills.

4. Track-specific learning

Each apprentice follows learning activities related to their selected pathway. For example, Data Analytics apprentices may focus on data analysis and visualisation, while IT apprentices may focus on troubleshooting, networks and technical support.

5. Career-development workshops

The programme includes workshops designed to strengthen professional capabilities, workplace communication, career planning and job-readiness skills.

6. Career-readiness support

Apprentices receive broader career support throughout the programme. Toward the end of the apprenticeship, participants are provided with time and space to prepare for their next professional or educational step.

Compensation and Benefits

The Google apprenticeship opportunities are paid. Apprentices receive hourly compensation for time spent in on-the-job training and related technical instruction.

The listed annual compensation ranges are:

Apprenticeship Track Listed Annual Pay Range
Data Analytics US$47,500–US$63,500
Digital Marketing US$47,500–US$63,500
Project Management US$54,000–US$72,000
Information Technology US$47,500–US$63,500
User Experience Design US$54,000–US$72,000

The listings indicate a 0% bonus target for the advertised roles.

Individual compensation may vary depending on factors such as:

  • Job-related skills.
  • Relevant experience.
  • Education.
  • Professional training.
  • Other qualifications considered by Google.

The programme also offers professional benefits beyond compensation, including:

  • Practical experience at Google.
  • Structured technical training.
  • Exposure to professional teams.
  • Career-development workshops.
  • Development of transferable skills.
  • A nationally recognised credential upon successful completion.
  • Career-readiness support.

Applicants should review the official job listing for the most current information about benefits, compensation and employment conditions.

Location and Work-Authorisation Considerations

The listed apprenticeship opportunities are based in the United States. Google states that participation requires applicants to be located in the United States for the duration of the programme.

This is an important consideration for applicants living outside the United States. The availability of an application link does not automatically confirm that Google will provide:

  • Visa sponsorship.
  • Immigration assistance.
  • Relocation support.
  • Travel funding.
  • Accommodation.
  • Work-authorisation arrangements.

Applicants should carefully review the official listing and any applicable employment or work-authorisation requirements before applying.

The opportunities are therefore most directly suited to candidates who can meet the programme’s United States location and employment requirements.

Application Requirements

Applicants must prepare an updated CV or résumé in English before beginning the application process.

Google’s listings instruct applicants to:

  1. Visit the official apprenticeship listing for the selected track.
  2. Click the “Apply” button.
  3. Access or create a Google Careers profile if required.
  4. Complete the application form.
  5. Upload one single document containing an updated résumé in the résumé section.
  6. Use PDF format where possible.
  7. Provide any additional information requested.
  8. Review all information carefully before submitting the application.

The résumé should clearly communicate the applicant’s relevant skills, practical experience and willingness to learn.

Depending on the selected track, applicants may consider highlighting:

  • Education and training.
  • Personal projects.
  • Volunteer experience.
  • Technical skills.
  • Digital tools used.
  • Communication and teamwork experience.
  • Leadership or coordination experience.
  • Problem-solving examples.
  • Relevant online courses.
  • Practical exposure to the selected field.
  • Evidence of curiosity and continuous learning.

Applicants should tailor their résumé to the apprenticeship they are applying for. For example, an IT applicant should highlight troubleshooting, computer, software or technical projects, while a Digital Marketing applicant may emphasise content creation, SEO, social media, campaign or analytics experience.

How to Apply

Interested applicants should apply through the relevant official Google Careers listing.

Data Analytics Apprenticeship

Apply for the Google Data Analytics Apprenticeship, February 2027 Start

Digital Marketing Apprenticeship

Apply for the Google Digital Marketing Apprenticeship, February 2027 Start

Project Management Apprenticeship

Apply for the Google Project Management Apprenticeship, February 2027 Start

Information Technology Apprenticeship

Apply for the Google Information Technology Apprenticeship, February 2027 Start

User Experience Design Apprenticeship

Apply for the Google User Experience Design Apprenticeship, February 2027 Start

Applicants should apply only through Google’s official careers platform and should verify the details of the selected listing before submitting an application.

Application Deadline

The deadline to apply for the February 2027 Google Apprenticeship opportunities is:

September 21, 2026

Applicants are encouraged to prepare and submit their applications early. Waiting until the final day may create unnecessary difficulties, especially if applicants need to create a profile, revise their résumé, resolve technical issues or complete several application sections.

Important Considerations Before Applying

Prospective applicants should take note of the following:

  • The programmes are full-time and require 40 hours per week.
  • The apprenticeships are expected to begin in February 2027.
  • The programme duration is approximately 18 months.

item.content:encoded:
The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) is inviting applications for a Communications Internship at its Rome Centre for Climate Action and Energy Transition in Rome, Italy.

This full-time internship offers an opportunity for students and recent graduates interested in communications, media, digital content, graphic design, marketing, climate action and sustainable development to gain practical experience within the United Nations system.

The internship will run for six months and will involve supporting the Rome Centre’s communications activities, including content development, digital communications, social media, event communications, website management, research and creative digital content.

The application deadline is 17 September 2026 at 03:59.

About the UNDP Communications Internship

The internship is based within the UNDP Rome Centre for Climate Action and Energy Transition, which focuses on areas including youth engagement in climate action, energy for development and climate finance.

The Rome Centre implements programmes including the Technical Assistance and Investment Support Facility, the Energy for Growth initiative and Youth4Climate.

These initiatives work to support climate and energy transitions, mobilize finance for sustainable development and strengthen youth participation in climate action.

As a Communications Intern, the successful candidate will support the Communications Lead across a range of communications and digital activities.

Key Areas of Work

1. Content Development

The intern will support the creation and editing of communications materials.

Responsibilities include:

  • Drafting and editing web stories.
  • Creating social media posts.
  • Supporting newsletters.
  • Preparing key messages and event blurbs.
  • Supporting the development of visual content for programmes and events.
  • Maintaining the Rome Centre’s media asset library.
  • Organizing photos, videos and graphics.
  • Supporting multilingual adaptation of content where relevant.

2. Digital Communications and Social Media

The intern will also contribute to the day-to-day management of the Rome Centre’s digital platforms.

This includes:

  • Supporting social media channels such as LinkedIn, Instagram and X.
  • Tracking content performance across different platforms.
  • Helping adapt stories and content to different platform formats.
  • Assisting with scheduling, drafting and posting.
  • Monitoring analytics and engagement.

3. Event Communications

The intern will support communications activities surrounding events and programmes.

Responsibilities may include:

  • Preparing event communications packages.
  • Developing visuals and hashtags.
  • Supporting photo and video briefs.
  • Providing live event coverage.
  • Gathering photographs, quotes and key takeaways.
  • Turning event materials into social media and web content after events.

4. Website Support

The selected intern will also gain experience supporting website communications.

Tasks include:

  • Drafting and formatting content for UNDP’s website.
  • Publishing content using the content management system.
  • Following UNDP’s brand and editorial guidelines.
  • Building and updating basic campaign and event pages.
  • Uploading and tagging media.
  • Writing alt text and captions.

5. Research and Creative Ideas

The internship will also involve supporting research and developing ideas for digital communications.

The intern may conduct desk research for campaigns and storytelling and contribute ideas for creative digital content and formats.

Eligibility Requirements

Applicants must meet one of the specified education requirements at the time of application.

Candidates may qualify if they:

  • Are enrolled in a postgraduate degree programme, such as a Master’s degree or higher, in Communications, Media Studies, Graphic Design, Marketing or a related field.
  • Are enrolled in the final academic year of a first university degree programme at bachelor’s level or equivalent in a related field.
  • Have recently graduated with a relevant university degree and, if selected, can begin the internship within one year of graduation.
  • Are enrolled in a postgraduate professional traineeship programme and will undertake the internship as part of that programme.

Required Skills and Experience

Applicants should have a strong understanding of digital media and how content works across major platforms.

Relevant experience and skills include:

  • Understanding of LinkedIn, Instagram, X and short-form video.
  • Ability to adapt content for different platforms.
  • Proficiency with social media tools and content management systems.
  • Familiarity with scheduling platforms.
  • Familiarity with basic analytics dashboards.
  • Experience with Canva, CapCut, Adobe Creative Suite or other design tools is an asset.
  • Interest in climate action, energy transition and sustainable development.
  • Knowledge of the UN system is an asset.

Important Portfolio Requirement

One of the most important requirements for this internship is the submission of a portfolio of relevant work.

UNDP states that applications will only be considered if they are accompanied by a portfolio.

Applicants should therefore ensure that their portfolio is included with their application and demonstrates relevant communications, digital media, design, social media, writing, video or other creative work.

Language Requirements

Applicants must have:

  • Excellent oral and written communication skills in English.
  • Working knowledge of Italian or another UN language is an asset.

What Happens If You Are Selected?

Successful applicants will be required to provide several documents electronically.

These may include:

  • A letter from their university confirming current enrollment and graduation date.
  • A university letter confirming sponsorship for the internship, where applicable.
  • A letter of recommendation from a professor.
  • Their most recent academic transcript.
  • A copy of their passport.
  • A completed UNDP Internship Application Form.
  • A signed UNDP Internship Agreement.
  • A Medical Certificate of Good Health.
  • Proof of medical insurance.
  • Their available internship period.

Internship Duration

The internship has a six-month contract duration and is a full-time internship programme based in Rome, Italy.

Internship Stipend

UNDP states that interns may receive a stipend under the applicable conditions.

Where an intern is not financially supported by another institution or programme, UNDP may provide a monthly stipend intended to help cover basic daily expenses related to the internship, such as meals and transportation at the duty station.

Where an intern receives external financial support, UNDP may pay the difference between that support and the applicable UNDP stipend, subject to the relevant rules.

Travel, Visa and Living Expenses

Applicants should note that costs and arrangements relating to travel, visas, passports, accommodation and living expenses are the responsibility of the nominating institution, related institution or government where applicable, or the intern.

Applicants should therefore carefully consider these costs before applying.

Medical Insurance

Interns are responsible for securing adequate medical insurance for the entire duration of their internship.

UNDP states that it will not reimburse the intern’s medical insurance costs.

Applicants who are neither nationals nor residents of the duty station must ensure that their insurance provides appropriate coverage for situations including medical treatment and, where necessary, transportation to their home country or country of residence.

Does the Internship Lead to Employment at UNDP?

The vacancy states that there is no expectation of employment with UNDP following completion of the internship.

Interns also cannot apply for or be appointed to another UNDP position during the period of their internship.

Diversity and Inclusion

UNDP states that diversity, equity and inclusion are core principles of the organization.

The organization encourages applications from people belonging to marginalized or excluded populations and emphasizes fairness, inclusion and representation in its workforce.

How to Apply for the UNDP Communications Internship 2026

Interested applicants should submit their application through the official UNDP recruitment platform.

Applicants should ensure that their application clearly demonstrates their relevant education, digital communications experience, creative skills and interest in climate action, energy transition and sustainable development.

Most importantly, candidates must include a portfolio of relevant work, as applications without a portfolio will not be considered.

Application Deadline

17 September 2026 at 03:59

The vacancy timeline indicates that the recruitment window is approximately one week, so eligible applicants are encouraged to apply as early as possible.

Conclusion

The UNDP Communications Internship 2026 in Rome, Italy offers an opportunity for students and recent graduates to gain practical experience in communications and digital media within an international development organization.

The six-month internship provides exposure to content development, social media, website management, event communications, research and creative digital communications while working within the UNDP Rome Centre for Climate Action and Energy Transition.

Candidates with relevant communications or creative backgrounds should pay particular attention to the portfolio requirement, as UNDP clearly states that applications will only be considered when accompanied by a portfolio of relevant work.

Eligible applicants should prepare their application and portfolio carefully and submit them before the 17 September 2026 deadline.

Discover more internship opportunities on the OFY Webpage.

item.content:encoded:
Applications are now open for the Caribbean Development Bank International Master in Public Procurement Management Scholarship 2026/2027, a major postgraduate funding opportunity for public procurement professionals from eligible Caribbean Development Bank Borrowing Member Countries.

The Caribbean Development Bank, commonly known as CDB, is supporting candidates to pursue the International Master in Public Procurement Management (IMPPM) at the University of Rome Tor Vergata in Italy during the 2026/2027 academic year. The programme is intended to strengthen public procurement capacity across the Caribbean, support the professionalisation of the public procurement workforce, and help participating countries modernise procurement systems in ways that improve value for money, integrity, accountability and development outcomes.

The scholarship package is extensive. It covers the full tuition fee, travel to and from Italy for the in-person study period, accommodation support, subsistence while in Italy, a USD 350 lump-sum allowance toward visa and other essential administrative costs, and in some cases reasonable travel costs associated with completing the visa process outside the applicant’s country of residence.

The application deadline is:

3 October 2026 at 5:00 PM Atlantic Standard Time (AST).

Applications must be submitted in PDF format by email to:

MasterIPPM@caribank.org

This opportunity is aimed at experienced public procurement professionals who are citizens of eligible CDB Borrowing Member Countries and who are currently employed in professional public procurement roles within government or eligible Caribbean public regional institutions.

About the Caribbean Development Bank Scholarship

The Caribbean Development Bank is offering this scholarship as part of its broader commitment to strengthening public financial management systems across its Borrowing Member Countries.

Public procurement plays a critical role in government performance because large amounts of public expenditure pass through procurement systems. Strong procurement institutions can help governments:

  • Improve value for money
  • Strengthen accountability
  • Reduce corruption risks
  • Improve transparency
  • Support sustainable development
  • Improve project delivery
  • Encourage fair competition
  • Advance inclusive procurement
  • Modernise public-sector purchasing

CDB views investment in procurement professionals as an important part of improving the development impact of both nationally financed and CDB-supported projects.

The 2026/2027 academic year marks the fifth consecutive year that CDB has supported this scholarship initiative.

What Is the International Master in Public Procurement Management?

The International Master in Public Procurement Management, or IMPPM, is a full-time postgraduate programme delivered by the:

Faculty of Economics, University of Rome Tor Vergata, Italy.

The programme is designed for professionals working in public procurement and related areas who want to develop deeper expertise in:

  • Procurement management
  • Procurement law
  • Procurement economics
  • Integrity
  • Anti-corruption
  • Negotiation
  • Sustainable procurement
  • Innovative procurement
  • Public-private partnerships
  • Procurement reform
  • Strategic procurement

The programme is delivered entirely in:

English.

Programme Structure

The programme runs for approximately one year and combines several different learning components.

These include:

  1. In-person classroom teaching in Rome
  2. Distance learning
  3. A mandatory professional internship
  4. A final dissertation

The academic model is therefore designed to combine theoretical learning with direct professional application.

In-Person Study in Rome

Students are expected to attend:

4.25 consecutive months of in-person classes in Rome.

The programme includes:

13 academic modules

covering important areas of public procurement.

Attendance is compulsory, and students are expected to participate actively in all modules. Each module concludes with an examination intended to assess the skills and knowledge acquired.

For professionals already employed in government or public institutions, this means employer support is particularly important.

Expected Start Date

The 2026/2027 edition is expected to begin in:

Early 2027.

The exact dates will be confirmed by the University of Rome Tor Vergata.

Applicants should therefore be prepared to arrange:

  • Employer release
  • Visa documentation
  • Travel
  • University documentation
  • CIMEA or Declaration of Value procedures

soon after selection.

Scholarship Benefits

The CDB scholarship offers a broad financial support package.

Full Tuition Fees

The scholarship covers:

The full tuition fee for the postgraduate programme.

The sponsoring organisation pays the tuition fee directly to the University.

Travel to and From Italy

The scholarship covers:

Travel costs to and from Italy

for the in-person phase of the programme.

It also provides:

A per diem while in transit.

This substantially reduces the financial barrier to attending the residential component in Rome.

Accommodation Support

Scholarship recipients receive:

An allowance for accommodation on campus at the University.

Applicants should understand that the notice describes this as an allowance, rather than simply stating that accommodation itself is automatically prepaid in full.

Living and Subsistence Allowance

The scholarship also provides:

An allowance for subsistence costs while in Italy.

This is intended to support the recipient’s living costs during the 4.25-month period in Rome.

The official notice does not state the exact amount of the subsistence allowance in the material provided, so applicants should not assume a specific monthly figure unless CDB confirms it separately.

USD 350 Administrative Allowance

Selected candidates also receive:

USD 350 as a lump-sum allowance

paid in advance after the scholarship award is confirmed.

This payment is intended to help cover costs such as:

  • Visa expenses
  • CIMEA documentation
  • Declaration of Value
  • Other essential administrative expenses required to study and travel to Italy

Additional Visa-Related Travel Support

Some selected candidates may need to travel outside their country of residence to complete the Italian visa process.

Where this is necessary, the scholarship may cover reasonable and necessary travel-related costs, including:

  • Economy airfare
  • Accommodation
  • Applicable per diem

for the minimum required visa-processing period.

These costs are arranged or reimbursed by the sponsoring organisation according to its applicable procedures.

Mandatory Professional Internship

A major part of the programme is the required:

500-hour professional internship.

The internship is normally completed within:

  • The participant’s home organisation, or
  • Another institution acceptable to the University

This component is designed to ensure that participants apply their new knowledge directly within a professional procurement environment.

Final Dissertation Requirement

Scholarship recipients must also prepare a:

Final dissertation

based on a case study addressing procurement issues relevant to:

  • Their organisation
  • Their country
  • The Caribbean region

This gives participants the opportunity to link academic learning to practical public-sector procurement challenges.

Potential dissertation themes might include:

  • Sustainable procurement
  • Procurement digitisation
  • Procurement transparency
  • Anti-corruption systems
  • Procurement law reform
  • Innovative procurement
  • Public-private partnerships
  • Procurement capacity building
  • Green procurement
  • Inclusive procurement

Applicants should expect their research to have direct professional relevance.

Employer Release Is Required

Because the in-person study period in Rome lasts approximately 4.25 months, candidates must be:

Formally released from their professional duties

for the full period of in-person study.

Their employer must also support their participation in:

  • Distance learning
  • Academic assignments
  • Other programme requirements

without conflicting professional obligations.

Shortlisted candidates will need written confirmation from their employer granting this release before proceeding to the second stage of evaluation.

Applicants are therefore strongly encouraged to speak with their employers before applying.

Post-Study Employment Commitment

Scholarship recipients must continue serving their employer for at least:

12 months after completing the programme.

This is a formal condition of the award.

An agreement must be reached between the scholarship recipient and their employer stipulating that the full tuition cost must be reimbursed if the recipient leaves before completing the required 12-month service period.

Applicants should therefore consider carefully whether they are willing and able to make this employment commitment.

Why the Return-to-Employer Requirement Matters

The scholarship is designed as a capacity-building investment.

CDB is not only funding an individual academic degree.

It is investing in:

  • Public-sector institutions
  • National procurement systems
  • Regional procurement expertise
  • Procurement reform
  • Knowledge transfer

The 12-month service requirement helps ensure that the knowledge gained through the programme is transferred back into the applicant’s professional environment.

Knowledge-Sharing After Graduation

Scholarship recipients are also expected to share what they have learned with colleagues in:

  • Their home country
  • Their institution
  • The broader Caribbean region

Possible activities may include:

  • Presentations
  • Training sessions
  • Professional discussions
  • Knowledge-sharing workshops

Topics could include:

  • Sustainable procurement
  • Digital transformation
  • Innovative procurement strategies

Approximately 6 to 12 months after graduation, CDB intends to follow up with scholarship recipients to assess the impact of the programme.

Who Can Apply?

Eligibility is relatively specific.

Applicants must satisfy both:

  • CDB scholarship requirements
  • University of Rome Tor Vergata admission requirements

Candidates should carefully review all conditions before applying.

Citizenship Requirement

Applicants must be citizens of one of the eligible CDB Borrowing Member Countries.

The eligible countries and territories listed in the official notice are:

  • Anguilla
  • Antigua and Barbuda
  • Barbados
  • Belize
  • British Virgin Islands
  • Cayman Islands
  • Dominica
  • Grenada
  • Guyana
  • Haiti
  • Jamaica
  • Montserrat
  • Saint Kitts and Nevis
  • Saint Lucia
  • Saint Vincent and the Grenadines
  • Suriname
  • The Bahamas
  • Trinidad and Tobago
  • Turks and Caicos Islands

Applicants from countries outside this list are not eligible under the published call.

Employment Requirement

Candidates must be employed:

At the time of application and throughout the programme

in a:

Professional public procurement role

within either:

  • The government of a CDB Client country, or
  • A Caribbean public regional institution

This scholarship is therefore not intended for people who are merely interested in procurement but are not professionally working in the field.

Academic Qualification

Applicants must hold at least:

A recognised Master’s-level university degree.

The degree must be equivalent to an Italian two-year:

Master of Science degree

such as the Italian:

  • Laurea Magistrale
  • Laurea Specialistica
  • Laurea vecchio ordinamento

Applicants should be prepared to provide documentation showing equivalency through the appropriate Italian recognition process where required.

Professional Experience Requirement

Applicants should normally have at least:

Five years of relevant procurement experience

including at least:

Two years in public-sector procurement.

This reflects the programme’s professional orientation.

It is designed for practitioners who already understand the basics of procurement and want to strengthen their strategic and technical expertise.

Can Applicants With Less Experience Apply?

Possibly.

The official notice contains an important flexibility provision stating that:

Applicants who are highly motivated but have:

  • Recently completed a Master’s degree, and/or
  • Limited procurement experience

may still be considered at the discretion of:

  • CDB
  • The University

This means five years of experience is the normal requirement, but there is limited discretion for exceptional candidates.

Applicants with less experience should therefore make a particularly strong case in their motivation letter.

English-Language Requirement

Candidates must be proficient in:

  • Written English
  • Spoken English

This is essential because the full Master’s programme is delivered in English.

The notice provided does not specify a mandatory IELTS, TOEFL or other standardized test score, so applicants should not assume one is required unless the University’s separate admission rules state otherwise.

Conflict-of-Interest Requirement

Applicants must not have:

Business or personal relationships with CDB or the University of Rome Tor Vergata

that would create:

  • An actual conflict of interest
  • A perceived conflict of interest

Applicants must also sign a declaration confirming that they meet the eligibility requirements and have no relevant conflict of interest.

One Candidate Per Country Rule

The CDB states that:

Only one candidate from the same country may receive a scholarship award in any given year.

This policy is intended to distribute the programme’s benefits more equitably across eligible Caribbean countries.

However, CDB reserves the right to make exceptions where there are insufficient eligible candidates.

Selection Criteria

Meeting the formal eligibility criteria does not guarantee selection.

The evaluation places particular emphasis on:

  • Relevant professional experience
  • Leadership potential
  • Ability to use the programme to improve procurement outcomes
  • Potential contribution to procurement modernisation
  • Capacity to apply knowledge in the applicant’s institution
  • Potential regional impact

CDB particularly highlights areas such as:

  • Sustainable procurement
  • Inclusive procurement

Leadership Potential

Applicants should demonstrate not only technical procurement experience but also the ability to:

  • Influence institutional change
  • Lead reform
  • Train colleagues
  • Strengthen procurement systems
  • Improve professional standards
  • Contribute to modernization

A strong application should therefore explain how the candidate will use the degree after returning home.

Sustainable and Inclusive Procurement

CDB specifically highlights:

Sustainable and inclusive procurement

as important areas for future procurement modernisation.

Applicants with relevant experience or future plans in areas such as:

  • Green procurement
  • Climate-conscious procurement
  • Social inclusion
  • SME participation
  • Gender-responsive procurement
  • Sustainable supply chains

may therefore have a strong opportunity to show programme relevance.

How to Apply

Applications must be submitted:

By email

to:

MasterIPPM@caribank.org

All documents must be submitted in:

PDF format.

Required Application Documents

Applicants must submit three core documents.

1. Updated Curriculum Vitae

The CV should clearly show:

  • Education
  • Procurement experience
  • Public-sector experience
  • Current employment
  • Leadership experience
  • Procurement reform experience
  • Relevant training
  • Professional certifications
  • Major projects
  • Regional or international experience

2. Motivational Cover Letter

Applicants must submit a:

Motivational cover letter

explaining their interest in the scholarship programme.

A competitive letter should explain:

  • Why public procurement matters to the applicant
  • Why the IMPPM is relevant to their current work
  • What procurement challenges exist in their country or institution
  • What reforms they hope to support
  • How they will apply the knowledge after graduation
  • How they will contribute to sustainable and inclusive procurement
  • How the scholarship will benefit their institution and country

3. Signed Eligibility Declaration

Applicants must submit a:

Signed Declaration

confirming that they meet all eligibility conditions.

This includes confirmation that there is no actual or perceived conflict of interest.

The required template is attached to the official Call for Applications and must be completed and signed.

Stage 1: Shortlisting

After the deadline, a CDB evaluation panel will review the applications.

The panel will shortlist up to:

Six candidates

who best satisfy the eligibility and qualification criteria.

Shortlisted candidates will then be contacted by the University for an interview.

At this stage, applicants may need to provide proof that their employer is willing to release them from work for the in-person programme period.

Stage 2: University Interview

The University of Rome Tor Vergata will interview shortlisted candidates to confirm their suitability for the Master’s programme.

In consultation with CDB, the University then identifies final candidates for scholarship awards.

There is one inconsistency in the official notice worth flagging: the overview says CDB is offering scholarships to two candidates, while the selection-stage section says the University will identify three candidates for scholarship awards.

Because the headline and overview explicitly describe two scholarships, applicants should treat two awards as the advertised number unless CDB issues clarification. Anyone needing certainty can contact CDB directly before applying.

Final Scholarship Confirmation

Successful candidates will receive:

  • An Admission Letter from the University
  • A Scholarship Offer Letter from CDB

The scholarship is formally confirmed once the recipient satisfies the University’s admission requirements.

Application Deadline

Applications must be received by:

3 October 2026 at 5:00 PM AST.

Applicants in other time zones should convert the deadline carefully.

Because applications are sent by email, it is advisable to submit before the final day and confirm that:

  • All files are attached
  • All files are readable
  • The Declaration is signed
  • Documents are PDFs
  • Email address is correct

How to Prepare a Strong Application

1. Connect Your Experience to Procurement Reform

Avoid writing only that you want another degree.

Explain what procurement problem you want to solve.

Possible examples include:

  • Inefficient procurement processes
  • Limited digitisation
  • Weak transparency
  • Delays in procurement
  • Limited sustainability standards
  • Weak supplier diversity
  • Public procurement capacity gaps

2. Demonstrate Leadership Potential

Because leadership is explicitly part of the selection criteria, show examples of situations where you have:

  • Led procurement processes
  • Improved systems
  • Coordinated teams
  • Introduced new procedures
  • Trained colleagues
  • Managed complex procurements

3. Explain the Regional Value

CDB is interested not only in individual development but also in wider Caribbean impact.

Where possible, explain how your learning could benefit:

  • Your institution
  • Your country
  • Other Caribbean procurement professionals

4. Highlight Sustainable Procurement

If you have experience involving:

  • Environmental criteria
  • Climate considerations
  • Social safeguards
  • Responsible sourcing

include it clearly.

Sustainable procurement is specifically highlighted in the selection criteria.

5. Discuss Employer Support Early

Do not wait until you are shortlisted to tell your employer you may need more than four months away from normal duties.

The official notice explicitly encourages applicants to discuss the possibility of employer release early.

6. Be Ready for the 12-Month Return Commitment

Applicants should understand before applying that they will be expected to remain with their employer for at least one year after completing the programme.

This is not a minor administrative detail.

It is part of the scholarship’s institutional-capacity-building model.

Key Details at a Glance

Programme: International Master in Public Procurement Management

University: University of Rome Tor Vergata

Country: Italy

Academic year: 2026/2027

Sponsor: Caribbean Development Bank

Advertised scholarship places: 2

Programme length: Approximately one year

In-person study: 4.25 consecutive months in Rome

Modules: 13

Language: English

Internship: 500 hours

Dissertation: Required

Tuition: Fully covered

Travel to/from Italy: Covered

Accommodation allowance: Included

Subsistence allowance: Included

Administrative allowance: USD 350

Visa-related travel: May be covered where necessary

Employer release: Required

Post-study service requirement: Minimum 12 months with employer

Application deadline: 3 October 2026, 5:00 PM AST

Application email: MasterIPPM@caribank.org

Questions: procurement@caribank.org

Conclusion

The Caribbean Development Bank International Master in Public Procurement Management Scholarship 2026/2027 offers experienced Caribbean public procurement professionals a rare opportunity to complete an internationally focused postgraduate programme at the University of Rome Tor Vergata with extensive financial support.

The scholarship covers full tuition, travel to and from Italy for the in-person academic period, accommodation and subsistence allowances, a USD 350 administrative allowance, and eligible visa-related travel costs where necessary.

The programme combines 4.25 months of classroom teaching in Rome, distance learning, a 500-hour professional internship and a final procurement-focused dissertation.

Applicants must normally be citizens of eligible CDB Borrowing Member Countries, work in professional public procurement within government or an eligible regional public institution, hold a recognised Master’s-level degree, possess at least five years of relevant procurement experience including two years in public-sector procurement, and be proficient in English.

The scholarship is especially suited to professionals who want to strengthen their expertise in procurement reform, sustainable and inclusive procurement, integrity, anti-corruption, procurement law, public-private partnerships and strategic public purchasing.

Applications must be submitted in PDF format to:  MasterIPPM@caribank.org   by:3 October 2026 at 5:00 PM AST.

The Cornell Collaboration for International Development Economics Research (CIDER) at Cornell University is inviting applications for its Pre-Doctoral Research Fellowship Program, a full-time, post-baccalaureate opportunity for individuals preparing for doctoral study in Economics, Agricultural and Resource Economics, Development Studies, Public Policy, or related disciplines.

The position is based at Cornell University’s Ithaca Main Campus in New York, USA, and provides fellows with hands-on experience in quantitative research, data analysis, academic research and professional development.

The programme is particularly suitable for graduates who intend to pursue a PhD and want to strengthen their research experience while working closely with Cornell faculty on development economics projects.

About the Cornell CIDER Pre-Doctoral Research Fellowship

The CIDER Pre-Doctoral Research Fellowship is a full-time, one-year staff position designed to prepare promising researchers for future doctoral studies.

Selected fellows will work closely with Cornell faculty members whose research broadly focuses on development economics. Their work may involve quantitative research, data analysis, research design, data collection and other activities supporting faculty-led research projects.

Depending on project requirements, language abilities and individual interests, fellows may also have opportunities to participate in field research.

The fellowship provides an academically rigorous environment where participants can gain practical research experience while becoming part of Cornell University’s intellectual community.

Cornell expects to recruit multiple fellows who will join a cohort alongside continuing CIDER pre-doctoral fellows.

The appointment may be renewed for up to two years, depending on performance and availability of funding.

About CIDER

The Cornell Collaboration for International Development Economics Research (CIDER) is a cross-campus initiative involving faculty from several Cornell University units, including the SC Johnson College of Business, College of Agriculture and Life Sciences, College of Arts and Sciences, and the Cornell Jeb E. Brooks School of Public Policy.

CIDER brings together faculty working across international development economics and related areas, including poverty, food insecurity, agricultural and rural development, labor markets, nutrition, resilience and structural transformation.

The initiative emphasizes rigorous applied research designed to generate evidence that can inform public and private decision-makers around the world.

Key Responsibilities

Successful candidates will contribute to a variety of research and academic activities.

Research Support

Responsibilities include:

  • Supporting faculty Principal Investigators and research teams in planning, designing and implementing research projects.
  • Assisting with research activities and data collection.
  • Collecting, cleaning, managing and analyzing secondary data.
  • Developing and maintaining research code used to organize and analyze data.
  • Supporting the design, implementation, monitoring and updating of research surveys.
  • Working with partner organizations involved in research implementation and data collection.
  • Conducting literature reviews and synthesizing research findings.
  • Assisting with manuscripts, conference presentations and research talks.
  • Supporting grant and funding reports, Institutional Review Board submissions and other research documentation.

Administrative Support

Fellows may also:

  • Prepare materials and resources for CIDER programmes, events and initiatives.
  • Provide logistical and administrative support for virtual and in-person training programmes, workshops and seminars.

Professional Development

The position also provides opportunities for fellows to:

  • Participate in research seminar series.
  • Engage in Cornell University’s broader intellectual community.
  • Participate in professional development and training opportunities.
  • Access research-related training through CIDER and other Cornell units.
  • Potentially serve as a teaching assistant for a related course by mutual agreement with supervising faculty.

Salary and Benefits

The Cornell CIDER Pre-Doctoral Research Fellowship is a paid full-time position.

The stated salary range is:

$65,447 – $75,632 per year

The actual hiring rate may depend on factors including prior relevant experience, education, applicable skills and academic discipline.

Cornell also lists a range of employee benefits, including:

  • Health care options
  • Retirement contributions
  • Wellness programmes
  • Employee discounts
  • Vacation and personal leave
  • Paid holidays
  • Winter break
  • Educational benefits
  • Tuition-related programmes
  • Professional development opportunities

Eligibility Requirements

Candidates should have a Bachelor’s degree in economics, business, public policy, mathematics, statistics or a related field, together with 2 to 4 years of relevant experience or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

Applicants should also have:

  • Previous coursework in econometrics and statistics.
  • Familiarity with statistical software such as Stata or R.
  • Strong knowledge of economics research techniques and/or methods.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
  • Ability to manage multiple projects.
  • Excellent professional verbal, written and presentation skills.
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively.
  • Ability to meet deadlines.
  • Ability to seek, coordinate and appropriately disseminate information.
  • Experience working directly with people from different socioeconomic backgrounds.
  • Experience incorporating perspectives from multiple communities.

Preferred Qualifications

The following qualifications are preferred but are not mandatory:

  • A Master’s degree in economics, business, public policy, mathematics, statistics or a related field.
  • Relevant research experience, such as a senior thesis.
  • Experience with additional data analysis, programming or GIS tools.
  • Knowledge of tools such as ArcGIS, Python or SQL.
  • Foreign-language proficiency, particularly in French, Spanish, Swahili, Tamil and/or Portuguese.

Visa and Work Location

The position is onsite at Cornell University’s Ithaca Main Campus in New York.

The posting states that individuals with F-1 OPT/STEM OPT can apply. It also states that no other visa sponsorship or relocation assistance is available for this position.

Who Should Apply?

This opportunity is particularly relevant to graduates who:

  • Have completed a Bachelor’s degree in a relevant discipline.
  • Want to pursue doctoral studies.
  • Are interested in development economics or related research fields.
  • Have quantitative research and data-analysis skills.
  • Have coursework or experience in econometrics and statistics.
  • Want to gain experience working with university researchers.
  • Are interested in academic research and potentially pursuing a PhD.
  • Have an interest in international development research.

Applicants should demonstrate their research interests, relevant quantitative research experience and skills, as well as their interest in pursuing doctoral study.

How to Apply

Applicants are required to submit a resume and cover letter explaining their research interests, relevant quantitative research experience and skills, and their interest in pursuing doctoral study.

Cornell indicates that most positions require applicants to apply online and submit both a resume/CV and cover letter.

Application Deadline

15 October 2026

Applications received by October 15, 2026, will receive full consideration. Applications submitted after this date may still be considered until the positions are filled.

Apply

Interested candidates should apply through the official Cornell University careers platform and follow the online submission instructions provided in the job posting.

Contact Information

Contact Name: Melissa Dorward-Bauman

Contact Email: msm298@cornell.edu

Why Consider This Opportunity?

The Cornell CIDER Pre-Doctoral Research Fellowship offers an opportunity for aspiring doctoral researchers to gain substantial practical experience before entering a PhD programme.

Participants can work alongside faculty researchers, contribute to development economics research, strengthen their quantitative research abilities and participate in seminars and professional development activities.

For graduates considering doctoral study in economics, development studies, public policy or related disciplines, the position can provide valuable exposure to the academic research environment and help strengthen their preparation for future PhD applications.

Conclusion

The Cornell CIDER Pre-Doctoral Research Fellowship 2026 is an excellent opportunity for qualified graduates seeking to build strong research experience before pursuing doctoral studies.

The full-time position combines hands-on research, quantitative data analysis, academic engagement and professional development at Cornell University in Ithaca, New York. Successful candidates will work with faculty on development economics research while gaining exposure to the wider intellectual life of one of the world’s leading research universities.

Qualified applicants should prepare a strong resume and cover letter highlighting their research experience, quantitative skills and doctoral ambitions, and submit their applications before the 15 October 2026 full-consideration deadline.
